## DG6 round 3: code-security review of candidate aa219bd2, verdict **PASS**

Both open findings are now closed and verified, and I raised no new findings. The candidate ID recomputes to `sha256:aa219bd2…cb14` over 2729 files, both at the start and at the end. HEAD was the freeze commit on top of source commit `95f9819`. During the run, HEAD moved once when the runner committed the domain reviewer's run records; no product paths changed, and I did not open those records.

### The two open findings
- **F-DG6-180 (High, mandatory): CLOSED_VERIFIED.** My round-2 reproduction, rerun unchanged, now passes: after a benefit is marked sensitive, its calculation lineage is no longer listed to the team lead. I extended it to check the other readers:
  - An auditor without access doesn't see the row; the transformation office does.
  - An explicit grant to the team lead shows it, and revoking the grant hides it again.
  - I reverted the fix two ways (removing the list filter, and removing the new sensitive-record mapping). The tests caught both.
- **F-DG6-181 (High, mandatory): CLOSED_VERIFIED.** My round-2 probe, rerun unchanged, now stops at its first step: with no IT binding file, even organization B's own connector is refused. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour. With IT's binding for B in place, every attack I tried was refused:
  - organization A naming B's secret, aimed at the attacker's host or at B's own bound host;
  - URL tricks (userinfo, host suffix, trailing dot, decimal IP, percent-encoding);
  - rotating a webhook secret to B's;
  - a storage connection test naming B's secret.

  A refusal for a real secret is identical to one for a name nobody set, so it reveals nothing. B's token only ever reached B's bound host. I reverted the fix three ways (organization not compared, no check when the setting is saved, no check when the secret is used); each was caught.

### The four D-210 points (none raised as a finding)
- **The secret binding** holds on every save and use path.
- **Omitting sensitive values from scenarios (BE-Z3)** is acceptable. Hidden values are left out, naming a hidden benefit gets the same 422 as an unknown one, and scenarios carry no totals.
- **Endpoints without credentials can still reach internal hosts.** This is an acceptable residual. Only a technical admin can set one, the connector is https-only, refuses redirects and parses a strict response shape, and D-209 leaves it to the documented network egress policy.
- **ADR-0011 omits the object store.** This is documentation drift with no behavioural effect. The operator-facing list in `restricted-network.md` is complete.

**One observation:** any technical admin may create organizations (a DG1 design choice). So an organization code that IT binds a secret to before the organization exists can be created by another organization's admin. The secret still goes only to its bound host.

### Checks run
- **Static and historical:** typecheck, lint, format, OpenAPI lint and the no-CDN scan all pass. The historical validators for DG5 to DG1 all pass.
- **Unit tests on Node 22 and Node 24:** pass. Every failure in the full runs was a timeout or a UI element wait under load of about 20–29 on 4 vCPUs (three reviews at once). Each failing file passes when run alone. On Node 22 the architecture test needed three solo runs: two passed every test but exited 1 because the test runner itself timed out internally under load; the third, at lower load, exited 0.
- **Integration suite, both locales:** all 416 files pass, after rerunning the failures alone.
  - The LANG-unset run hit the 2-hour background limit while its first shard was unfinished. I ran the 9 files neither shard had completed separately, and all pass.
  - Its failures were timeouts, one shutdown-timing test, and an outbox relay test that counted 5 extra events, which I judge to be other tests' events under load. All pass alone.
  - The C.UTF-8 run's 5 failures (timeouts, plus a test API process that didn't start in time) also pass alone.
  - The contract test reports 932 of 932 operations validated, and every `p6-pending` list is empty.
- **Deferred e2e specs** (A17 failing connector, A17 import and webhook, A12 scope isolation including the assistant): 24 of 24 pass in both languages.
- **Role sweeps:** AUD is refused all 128 writes it tries. An ADM-only user gets no 200 on any of 126 transformation-scoped reads.
- **Environmental residuals** (live registry and CI, Keycloak, external systems, production capacity) are recorded as the assignment directs.

**Note:** `git status` in my sandbox shows the domain reviewer's three round-3 files as deleted. That comes from the sandbox's private staging copy of the reviews folder; I never touched those files.

All work ran in disposable clones, which I removed with no implementation file changed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- reviews/DG6/round-3/code-security-reviewer.json
- reviews/DG6/round-3/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json
- test-evidence/DG6/code-security/round-3/ (logs, `checks.sh`, and the probes under `repro/`)
